reason: The same-witness step from the handoff pattern's roleFibre membership to its fixed canonical charge t and role r is sound, and the boundaryWindow, crossWindow, remainder, and primitive token clauses are broadly described correctly. The submitted novel physical-support case is vacuous, however. If a pair has a sharedLocalBuffer blocker at vertex v, then v lies in both demands' localBuffer sets. Each localBuffer is a subset of its declaredSupport, so the blocker family also contains sharedDeclaredSupport (vertex v). canonicalBlocker scans all sharedDeclaredSupport candidates before any sharedLocalBuffer candidate; consequently no charged pair can have canonical blocker kind sharedLocalBuffer, and a nonempty same-role handoff pattern cannot realize the proposed primitiveVertex/sharedLocalBuffer branch. The note treats that branch as a live unresolved interaction with both actual T(p), so it fails the Phase 2 requirement for a supported new relation. In addition, the result's phrase 'fixed canonical blocker carrier' overstates the first three token clauses: their fixed edge or vertex is selected from the blocker's declared support, while only the primitive clause is defined by the blocker's carrier. A repair could retain the valid charge inventory and examine a live sharedDeclaredSupport case, whose guaranteed membership is in both declared supports T(p) union Gamma(p), without asserting membership in both local buffers. No separate window-class witness equality is used.
